Parsnips — Architecture & Data Schema

Singapore Parliament, snipped. This page describes how the system is designed, with focus on the data schema and verification chain.

1. Module Architecture

scraper parsnips_fetch.py

API client. Fetches sittings from the Parliament portal. Handles the three POST endpoints, speaker-name parsing, and the maxResult trap. Stdlib only.

scraper backfill.py

Year-batched ingestion. Resumable, parallel, discovers sitting dates. One batch = one year. Interrupted runs lose only in-flight sittings.

scraper storage.py

Single source of truth for paths. Year-sharded storage, stable keys, manifest. Imported by fetcher, summariser, and site builder so they cannot drift.

scraper normalise.py

Raw parse → canonical schema. Converts raw HTML to speaker-attributed turns. Handles the four traps: maxResult, split debates, speaker names, bare-name references.

summariser summarise.py

LLM summarisation. Map-reduce over chunks. Each chunk emits key_points with citations. Reduce produces item-level fields. Resumable, parallel.

summariser build_briefs.py

Brief assembly. Turns chunk notes into published briefs. Schema 4: selection-by-sentence-id. Every published sentence byte-identical to the record.

summariser build_dataset.py

Dataset builder. Builds the per-item dataset from sittings. Chunks at turn boundaries, sub-splits long turns at sentence boundaries.

rag export_read.py

Site builder. Builds the deployed static site → site/dist/. 331 pages, ~30s. The only thing that produces deployable output.

rag read_server.py

Reading view. Local server with working ask box. Port 8444. Uses the same RAG pipeline as the deployed site.

rag answer.py

Ask pipeline. Retrieves relevant chunks, generates answers with citations. Every answer traceable to source sentences.

tools verify_sitting.py

Completeness checker. Compares stored data against a fresh Hansard pull. Levels: 1a reports, 1b sentences, 2 extraction. Selftest plants known defects.

tools verify_summaries.py

Summary quality verifier. LLM-based, checks summaries against their own sentences. Four failure modes: unsupported, wrong_scope, question_as_finding, wrong_speaker.

tools check_selection.py

Verbatim invariant. Proves every published sentence is byte-identical to the record. Checks: text mismatches, unresolved sids, inferred speakers, duplicates, empty sections.

tools test_deterministic.py

Deterministic test suite. Selftest + completeness vs live source + secondary verifier. Exit 0 only when selftest catches every planted defect AND every sitting passes AND secondary check runs.

tools test_verifier.py

Verifier calibration. Tests the citation verifier against real and injected cases. A verifier that cannot find known defects is manufacturing confidence.

2. Data Flow

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ Parliament Portal (sprs.parl.gov.sg) │ │ POST /searchResult · POST /getHansardTopic · POST /fetchData │ └──────────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ ▼ scraper/parsnips_fetch.py (API client, speaker parsing) │ ▼ scraper/backfill.py (year-batched, resumable) │ ▼ scraper/storage.py (year shards, manifest) │ ┌──────────────┼──────────────┐ ▼ ▼ ▼ scraper/normalise.py summariser/ rag/build_dataset.py (canonical schema) build_dataset (chunking) │ │ │ └──────────────┼──────────────┘ ▼ summariser/summarise.py (map-reduce, LLM) │ ▼ summariser/build_briefs.py (schema 4, selection-by-sid) │ ▼ tools/check_selection.py (verbatim invariant gate) │ ▼ rag/export_read.py (static site → site/dist) │ ▼ Vercel (331 pages live)

3. Data Schema

3.1 Sitting

One calendar day Parliament sits. The top-level unit of the archive.

type Sitting = {
  date: string              // ISO YYYY-MM-DD
  year: string              // "2016"–"2026"
  parliament: number        // e.g. 14
  volume: number
  sitting_no: number
  format: string            // "sprs3"
  report_count: number
  words: number
  turns: number
  coverage_ratio: number    // stored vs fresh
  speaker_attribution_rate: number
  groups: {                 // per-type split
    oral: number
    written: number
    bill: number
    motion: number
    budget: number
    ...
  }
  source_hash: string       // content hash
  summarised: number        // how many briefs done
}

3.2 Report

One record in the Hansard API. A debate may span several reports. Reports carry the format era so a source link never infers it.

type Report = {
  reportId: string          // "oral-answer-4213"
  title: string
  type: string              // "oral" | "written" | "bill" | "motion" | "budget" | ...
  parliament_no: number
  sitting_no: number
  volume_no: number
  report_version: string    // "sprs3"
  words: number
  turns: Turn[]
}

type Turn = {
  speaker: string | null    // null = unattributed (4%)
  text: string
  words: number
}

3.3 Item

A policy item: one report, or several merged because they are the same business on consecutive sitting days. The unit of summarisation.

type Item = {
  report_ids: string[]      // ["motion-3008", "motion-3010"]
  title: string
  type: string
  sentences: Sentence[]     // flattened from all reports
}

type Sentence = {
  sid: string               // "s00012" — stable across the pipeline
  speaker: string | null
  text: string
  words: number
}

3.4 Brief (Schema 4)

The published summary of one item. Selection-by-sentence-id: every published sentence references its source by sid, never by copied text.

type Brief = {
  schema: 4
  what_it_is: string
  sections: Section[]
  _meta: {
    report_ids: string[]
    gate: {
      passed: boolean
      coverage: number      // selection share
    }
    selection_share: number
    sections_total: number
    source_words: number
  }
}

type Section = {
  label: string
  summary: string
  sentences: PublishedSentence[]
}

type PublishedSentence = {
  sid: string               // references Item.sentences
  speaker: string | null
  text: string              // byte-identical to source
  attributed: boolean       // false = inferred
  added_for_context: boolean
}

3.5 Storage Layout

data/
  manifest.json             // what exists, what is summarised, what is stale
  sittings.json             // flat site-facing index
  2016/sitting_2016-03-01.json
  2026/sitting_2026-08-05.json

summaries/
  index.json                // flat index for the site
  2016/motion-3008+3010.json
  2026/oral-answer-4213.json

pipeline/                   // gitignored derived data
  dataset//.json
  verification.jsonl
  summary_verify_cache.jsonl

site/dist/                  // the deployed site (tracked)
  index.html
  2016/sitting_2016-03-01.html
  ...

4. Key Design Decisions

Correctness Over Completeness

Where the two conflict, publish less. A wrong citation is worse than a missing point. Unverifiable items are withheld entirely, not published with a disclaimer.

Selection by Sentence ID

Every published sentence references its source by sid, never by copied text. This makes fabrication impossible in principle — the verbatim invariant is checkable by a script.

Fail-Closed Gates

Unknown or unvalidated state results in non-publication. A gate that reports and lets the item through is worse than no gate — it manufactures confidence.

Independent Verifier

The verifier is a different model family from the pipeline. The pipeline is deepseek-v4.1-flash:cloud; the verifier is gpt-oss:20b-cloud. A model checking its own output tends to agree with itself.

Stable Keys, Not Titles

Briefs are keyed by report identity, never by title. Titles are not unique (Hansard splits debates across records) and they change. Report ids are the real identity.

JSON as Source of Truth

The archive is JSON, not a database. Every sitting is a reviewable, citable commit. A database queries faster but turns the archive into a binary blob.

Map-Reduce Summarisation

Chunks emit key_points only. A chunk cannot know the item's title or significance, so it is not asked for them — asking would invitation invention. Item-level judgement belongs in the reduce step.

Information-Preserving Ingestion

Speaker identities are not resolved during ingestion. Grouping is by the recorded label. Identity resolution is a later concern built on preserved data, not folded into ingestion.

5. Verification Chain

The verification chain is the quality process. There is no human in the loop — the gates ARE the quality process.

Stage Tool What it checks Fail mode
gate 1 check_selection.py Verbatim invariant: every published sentence byte-identical to the record. Also: unresolved sids, inferred speakers, duplicates, empty sections. Hard fail. Item withheld.
gate 2 verify_summaries.py Summary quality: does the summary accurately describe its own sentences? Four failure modes: unsupported, wrong_scope, question_as_finding, wrong_speaker. Hard fail. Item withheld.
gate 3 verify_sitting.py Completeness vs live source: stored data against a fresh Hansard pull. Levels: 1a reports, 1b sentences, 2 extraction. Hard fail. Sitting flagged.
gate 4 test_deterministic.py Selftest + completeness + secondary verifier. Plants known defects and asserts the checker catches them. Hard fail. Suite exits non-zero.
gate 5 test_verifier.py Verifier calibration: tests the citation verifier against real and injected cases. Hard fail. Verifier replaced.
Selftest principle: a gate that has never been observed failing has not been shown to work. Every gate has a test that deliberately violates it and asserts the failure is caught. A checker whose own selftest has gone green-by-accident is the exact failure this project keeps producing.

6. Testing Methodology

6.1 Test Layers

Layer Tool What it tests
selftest verify_sitting.py --selftest Plants known defects (dropped report, merged turn, altered word, shifted dataset) and asserts the checker catches every one.
completeness verify_sitting.py Every sitting's stored data against a fresh pull from Hansard. No cache is reused.
secondary test_deterministic.py A model that is NOT the implementor model reviews the deterministic evidence. Its job: is the evidence self-consistent and specific enough to act on?
verbatim check_selection.py Every published sentence byte-identical to the record. Structural emptiness is a defect, not an absence.
quality verify_summaries.py LLM-based, checks summaries against their own sentences. Stratified sampling: random + longest + thinnest + multi-report.
calibration test_verifier.py Tests the citation verifier against real and injected cases. A verifier that cannot find known defects is manufacturing confidence.

6.2 Testing Principles

Selftest First

The negative control runs FIRST. It plants known defects into a real sitting and asserts the checker catches every one, plus that an unmodified sitting passes.

Deterministic Before Probabilistic

Mechanical checks (ids, set membership, text equality) are never overridden by a model. A probabilistic layer with discretionary control over deterministic evidence is how a PASS was once fabricated.

Stratified Sampling

Random-only sampling under-covers exactly the cases a correctness check exists to find. The sample is stratified: random + longest summaries + thinnest coverage + multi-report pages.

Deterministic Falsification

If the verifier quotes the words it calls invented, and those words appear in the section's own sentences, the flag is provably wrong — the material is present. A model's judgement is not checkable; a substring is.

Absence Is Not a Pass

If the verifier cannot be reached, the secondary check is recorded as not_run and the suite exits non-zero. An unverified state is not a verified one.

Real Cases, Not Invented

Test cases are REAL, taken from the archive and from defects this build actually produced — not invented to be easy. Each case carries the expected verdict class.

6.3 Example: Selftest

The selftest plants known defects into a real sitting and asserts the checker catches every one:

# The negative control, run FIRST
python3 tools/verify_sitting.py --selftest

# Planted defects:
#   - a dropped report
#   - a merged turn
#   - an altered word
#   - a one-sid shifted dataset

# Asserts:
#   - the checker catches every planted defect
#   - an unmodified sitting passes

6.4 Example: Verbatim Invariant

The verbatim invariant makes fabrication impossible in principle:

# Every published sentence must be byte-identical to the record
python3 tools/check_selection.py summaries/2026 2026

# Checks:
#   1. VERBATIM INVARIANT   text mismatches vs the record
#   2. SID RESOLUTION       ids with no record entry
#   3. SPEAKERS             inferred (attributed, blank)
#   4. DUPLICATES           same sentence twice
#      empty sections
#      sections without a summary
#      briefs with NO sections at all

6.5 Example: Stratified Sampling

The summary quality verifier uses stratified sampling to cover the cases most likely to be wrong:

# 40% random + 20% longest + 20% thinnest + 10% multi-report
python3 tools/verify_summaries.py --sample 400

# Four failure modes:
#   unsupported        the summary asserts something its sentences do not say
#   wrong_scope        the summary describes a different part of the record
#   question_as_finding a question is reported as a finding
#   wrong_speaker      a statement is attributed to a speaker who did not make it
